title: Decapod sperm-cell shape is an intermediate phase of osmotic shrinkage

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Decapod sperm-cell shape is an intermediate phase of osmotic shrinkage

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The normal form of decapod crustacean sperm-cells is one of many intermediate phases of shrinkage from a spherical form, caused by osmotic withdrawal of fluid without a matching reduction of surface area, so that equivalent shapes are produced by salt solutions of equivalent (molecular-weight-proportional) concentration.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. V: The Forms of Cells

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: we see that what we call its normal appearance is just one of many intermediate phases of shrinkage, brought about by the abstraction of fluid from its interior as the result of an osmotic pressure greater outside than inside the cell

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter V, “The Forms of Cells”; topic “Osmotic shapes of sperm-cells”. Scope: sperm-cells of decapod crustacea (Inachus, Galathea, Dromia, crayfish) and, by comparison, red blood cells

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch05-25: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.59

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The claim specifies an intervention, quantitative dose equivalence, and geometric mechanism. Public morphology can test whether normal forms resemble shrinkage states, but the decisive concentration-series data are scattered or absent.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Order decapod sperm shapes along measured osmotic concentration series and test whether volume loss at nearly constant surface area reproduces normal forms and collapses by solute molarity.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Public images rarely include controlled osmolarity metadata.

Species coverage for decapod sperm is limited.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
discriminating power: 0.78
operationalizability: 0.9
analysis feasibility: 0.62
data adequacy: 0.28
data existence: 0.42

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The claim states a clear experimental pattern: normal sperm shape is one frame of an osmotic shrinkage sequence, and equivalent osmolarities match. That pattern would discriminate osmotic collapse from a fixed cytoskeletal mould. The required concentration series is not in a public dataset, so the test cannot be run on existing downloads.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Place decapod sperm in a graded osmotic series and in equiosmolar salts of different molecular weight, and record the shape sequence from the sphere. Support would be a single shrinkage pathway ordered by osmolarity, with matching shapes at molecular-weight-proportional concentrations; stable species-specific shapes across that series would refute the claim.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Isolated micrographs of crustacean sperm lack the paired external concentration and surface-area measurements the test needs.

No public osmotic series exists for the named genera Inachus, Galathea, Dromia and crayfish.
